# How muscles work

## Muscles are machines that

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Generate forces in one direction
- Involuntary
  - Cardiac & smooth
- Voluntary
  - Striated
  - Skeletal
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](http://graphics8.nytimes.com/images/2007/08/01/health/adam/19917.jpg){fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Functional classes

- Axial
    + Trunk, neck, hips
- Proximal
    + Shoulder/elbow, pelvis/knee
- Distal
    + Hands/fingers, feet/toes

## Agonist/antagonist pairs {.scrollable}

![](http://2.bp.blogspot.com/-TpOC4my_NBc/T0J-MhEv29I/AAAAAAAAF88/dYLv7QzFwmg/s1600/Hamstring-Quad4.jpg){fig-align="center"}

## How skeletal muscles contract

- Motor neurons (cell bodies located in ventral horn of spinal cord)
- Project to muscle fiber(s)
  - Motor neuron + muscle fibers = *motor unit*
- Form *neuromuscular junction*
    + Synapse between motor neuron and muscle fiber
    + Release acetylcholine (ACh)

## Skeletal muscle fiber types

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Fast twitch/fatiguing
    + Type II
    + White meat
- Slow twitch/fatiguing
    + Type I
    + Red meat
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](../include/img/turkey.jpg){fig-align="center"}
:::
::::
    
## Muscles are sensory organs, too!

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Extrafusal fibers generate force
- Intrafusal fibers contain stretch receptors
  - Sense muscle length/tension
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](../include/img/muscle-fiber-types.jpg){fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Intrafusal fibers

+ Sense muscle length and change in length, e.g. "stretch"
+ Also called muscle spindles
+ Provide muscle proprioception (perception about the self, a form of interoception)

## Intrafusal fibers

- Muscle spindles are stretch receptors
  - Ennervated by by primary Ia afferents (sensory output from muscle)
  - Secondary Type II fibers
- Motor fiber
  + Ennervated by gamma ($\gamma$) motor neurons (motor input)

## Extrafusal fibers

+ Generate force
+ Ennervated by alpha ($\alpha$) motor neurons
  
## Monosynaptic stretch (myotatic) reflex

- Muscle stretched (length increases)
- Muscle spindle in intrafusal fiber activates
- Ia afferent $\rightarrow$ spinal cord
    + Activates alpha ($\alpha$) motor neuron
- $\alpha$ motor neuron activates extrafusal fiber
- Muscle contracts, shortens length

---

![Source: Wikipedia](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cd/Fusimotor_action.jpg)

- Gamma ($\gamma$) motor neuron fires to take up 'slack' in intrafusal fiber 

![](../include/img/intrafusal-extrafusal-fibers.jpg)

---

![](../include/img/stretch-reflex.jpg)

---

::: {.callout-note}
This is a bit like the role of a belayer in rock climbing.

![](https://www.thoughtco.com/thmb/_EukGM8OC9Rexe4KxtQxDQ3CsGs=/768x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():format(webp)/HowtoBelay_3-571117903df78c3fa293859d.jpg)
:::

---

```{mermaid}
%%| title: Nervous system output
%%| label: fig-info-flow-skeletal-muscle
%%| fig-cap: "CNS activation of skeletal muscle fibers."
flowchart TD
N{Nervous System} ==>|Alpha motor neurons|B(Extrafusal muscle fibers)
N ==>|Gamma motor neurons|C(Intrafusal muscle fibers)
C ==>|Ia spindle afferents|N
C ==>|Secondary afferents|N
```

## Why doesn't antagonist muscle respond?

- Contract bicep $\rightarrow$ stretch tricep

::: {.fragment}
- Polysynaptic inhibition of antagonist muscle
- Prevents/dampens tremor
:::

## "Tuning" proprioceptive feedback

:::{.callout-important}
## Developmental orgins
How does the motor system "learn" the sensory consequences of muscle fiber contraction?
Could spontaneous "twitches" be involved [@Blumberg2023-ce]?

That is, higher levels of the nervous system learn the relationship between motor neuron output and spindle feedback.
:::

## Speed

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- $\alpha$ motor neuron ~ 50-60 m/s
- Ia afferents ~ 80-120 m/s
- Brain to toe or toe to brain: 15-30 ms
- @Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Wikipedia-contributors2025-xk](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/bf/Nerve_Conduction_Velocity_Calculation.gif)
:::
::::

## Interim summary

- Voluntary movements involve contracting agonist or antagonist pairs of skeletal muscles
- Skeletal muscles have embedded sensors that detect length/tension
- CNS gets rapid feedback about muscle status
- Monosynaptic stretch (myotatic) reflexes maintain position stability

# Illustrative motor systems

## Looking

- Behavioral goals
  - Direct gaze (eyes + head + body) toward goal-relevant targets
  - Direct gaze toward emergent targets
  - Track/pursue targets across observer/target motion
  - Maximize quality of visual information about targets

## Saccades

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=40%}
- Rapid, ballistic (no online feedback)
- ~2-3/s
- ~200 ms to initiate
- Amplitudes >20 deg $\rightarrow$ saccade + head movement
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
{{< video https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e9/This_shows_a_recording_of_the_eye_movements_of_a_participant_looking_freely_at_a_picture.webm >}}

:::
::::

-- @Wikipedia-contributors2025-mr

## Smooth pursuit

![@Farnsworth2019-ux](https://imotions.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Smooth-pursuit-eye-tracking-2.png)

## Vergence

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=40%}
- Eyes move disjointly
- Fixate on comparable locations
- Binocular vision $\rightarrow$ 3D depth
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
![@Farnsworth2019-ux](https://imotions.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Vergence-2-1.png)
:::
::::

## Vestibulo-occular reflex (VOR)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=40%}
- Steady eyes when head moves
- Fast: response < 10 ms
- Disturbed in vertigo
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
![By .Koen - Own work based on: Simple vestibulo-ocular reflex.PNG and Image:ThreeNeuronArc.png, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=4130081](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Vestibulo-ocular_reflex_EN.svg/1280px-Vestibulo-ocular_reflex_EN.svg.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Considerations

::: {.incremental}
- Sensory feedback
  - Move eyes $\rightarrow$ shift visual field
  - Change vergence or lens thickness $\rightarrow$ change image focus
  - Eye muscles (probably) have proprioceptors analogous to spindles in skeletal muscles

:::

::: {.incremental}
- Relatively simple physics:

- Small # of muscles $\rightarrow$ "model" motor system?
- **DEMO**: Illustration of "forward"/generative model/[unconscious inference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconscious_inference)?
  - Predicting future/interpreting current sensory states
- Converging inputs: voluntary and involuntary control

## Interim summary

- Many (most?) behaviors involve multiple components
- Parallel, coordinated outputs to multiple motor systems
- Direct cortical control over eyes, fingers, vocal apparatus
- Feedback critical, often multisensory
